thread.title: Morning Movers: Facebook Slumps, Newell Gains, Apple Hits Universal Display

author: Barron's
title: Morning Movers: Facebook Slumps, Newell Gains, Apple Hits Universal Display
text:
The Dow is down this morning but it's the Nasdaq that's getting hit hard. In today's Morning Movers , we...
•...wonder if the market can survive without tech's leadership; •...why Newell Brands ( NWL ) is rising and Universal Display ( OLED ) is falling; •...and hear from a tech investors touting the strength of the sector.
If you live by the FANGs, you die by the FANGs, as the market is learning this morning.
Getty Images As we wrote earlier, reports that Facebook ( FB ) customer data was misused has caused its shares to tumble 4.3% to $177.20 in pre-open trading this market, and taken the tech sector with it . The Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF ( XLK ) is off 0.9% at $69.01 this morning.
No sector has been stronger than tech during the past three months--it's gained 8.5% to the S&P 500's 2.6% during the same time period--so it shouldn't come as a surprise that it's weakness is causing the market to fall today. Now, investors must decide if:
1)... Facebook's problem is a short-term one ; 2)...Whether it's a sign of a shift out of tech; 3)...and what, if anything, can claim leadership if tech's days are numbered.
The latter was a concern even before the Facebook news hit. "If technology is the only area of current leadership, and that begins to soften, that leaves the market vulnerable," MKM's Jonathan Krinsky stated over the weekend, noting that tech was the only sector with a positive return since the S&P 500's peak on Jan. 26.
In The Trader column this weekend, I offered up banks as a possible leadership group , but much will depend on what the Federal Reserve does on Wednesday, and what happens to interest rates.
Right now, though, it's anyone's guess.
S&P 500 Futures : -0.5% DJIA Futures : -132 points, or 0.5% Nasdaq Futures : -1.1%
AstraZenca ( AZN ) is up 0.9$ to $34.89 after Jefferies upgraded it to Buy.
Canadian Solar (CSIQ) is up 4.9%to $16.25 on its fourth-quarter earnings . The solar company said it earned $1.01 a share on revenue of $1.11 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 95 cents a share on revenue of $1.06 billion. For the full year, it sees revenues coming in between $4.4 billion and $4.6 billion, ahead of the $3.98 billion consensus.
Facebook ( FB ) is down 3.7% to $138.72 on news that the data firm Cambridge Analytica harvested the private data of millions of users, and still owns much or all of it.
Getty Images GrubHub (GRUB) is down 2.1% to $108.20 after Stifel cut it to Hold.
KLA-Tencor Corp (KLAC) is down 0.9% to $119.50 on news that it will buy Israeli electronics tech firm Orbotech (ORBK) in a $3.4 billion deal. It also announced a $2 billion share repurchase authorization.
Newell Brands ( NWL ) is up 4.2% to $29.85 after Carl Icahn disclosed a 6.86% active stake and that he the home products company had reached a deal that includes four new independent directors for its board.
Unilever (UN) is up 3.6% to $53.37 after Goldman Sachs upgraded it to Buy.
Universal Display ( OLED ) is down 6.5% to $116, and Synaptics (SNYA) is down 2.8% to $46.50 on news that Apple (AAPL) is developing its own iPhone screen . - Teresa Rivas
Bipul Sihna is as good a source as any when handicapping the state of the tech market.
Chief Executive Officer of enterprise start-up Rubrik, one of the fastest-growing companies in Silicon Valley, he's a former partner at venture-capital firm Lightspeed Partners and, before that, worked on mergers and acquisitions at Bank of America's Technology Investment Banking Group.
And, thankfully, he's opinionated.
Getty Images "The tech economy has been particularly strong with tax cuts and repatriation," says Sihna, who is especially bullish on cloud computing, artificial intelligence and Internet of Things. "This will buoy the stock market."
(Sihna's sentiment is shared by Daniel Ives, head of technology research at GBH Insights. Ives predicts tech stocks will rise 12% to 15% the rest of 2018, and remain "robust" for 12 to 18 months, thanks to FAANG members and enterprise cloud companies.) It all makes for an advantageous financial climate to go public, as Dropbox and Spotify plan to do shortly, and an active mergers-and-acquisition market, as Amazon (AMZN) recently proved with its purchase of Ring for a reported $1 billion , according to Sihna.
"I expect the tech IPO market to be very strong," says Sihna, pointing to the example of Dropbox's financial strength. The cloud-storage company disclosed it has annual revenue of $1.1 billion and about 11 million users. As for reports that Dropbox's market valuation as a public company will fall significantly short of its $10 billion assessment when private, Sihna dismissed them as "a bit carried away."
Sihna, whose company recently named Microsoft (MSFT) Chairman John Thompson to its board and is on pace for a $300 million run-rate, also expects plenty of tech stock buybacks to boost share prices in 2018. - Jon Swartz
